QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah's Category I Venture Capital AIF is interested in a teaser received from an investee company. Before the investee's investment banker releases the Confidential Information Memorandum (CIM), what is the MOST critical document the fund must typically execute?

explanation.text: The Logic: XIX-D pp. 220-225 describes the standard deal sequence: once a teaser is found interesting, the investment team negotiates and signs an NDA so the investee's investment banker can share the CIM/IM. In proprietary-sourced opportunities, the fund may sign an NDA directly with the target. The Trap: Term sheets come much later, after business diligence and the IC "go-ahead". SHA and SSA are definitive agreements executed at closing — long after the CIM is reviewed. Note: The pages checked do not extend the standard NDA to a "two-way" NDA, evaluation-IP protections, standstill clauses, or restrictions on the company approaching the AIF's LPs, so those add-ons are omitted.
